advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a render-site test asserting a CHANGE_INPUT outcome with diagnostic['finish_reason']=='content_filter' emits CONTENT_FILTER_MESSAGE to stderr through _disposition_exit_code / _llm_error_exit_code / the close_precheck hint.
evidence: ABSENCE: `search_files finish_reason` over tests/unit returns hits only in message_for unit tests (test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py) and unrelated classifier/runner tests; none assert a content-filter diagnostic reaching stderr via _disposition_exit_code / _llm_error_exit_code / close_precheck.
Existing _disposition_exit_code tests (test_plan_review_reuse.py:204-213, test_review_flags.py:133) assert exit codes, not stderr message content, and use no content_filter diagnostic.
advisory.finding: The new finish_reason plumbing at the three render sites (_llm_error_exit_code, _disposition_exit_code in _llm_commands.py, and the close_precheck except-arm) is not covered by any test: no test asserts that an outcome/coverage carrying diagnostic['finish_reason']=='content_filter' on a CHANGE_INPUT class causes the guardrail CONTENT_FILTER_MESSAGE (rather than the generic size/malformed message) to be written to stderr. message_for is unit-tested in isolation, but the diagnostic->finish_reason extraction wired at the call sites is not exercised, so a regression at that seam (wrong dict key, dropped kwarg) would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor changes the diagnostic key name or drops the finish_reason kwarg at a render site; message_for unit tests stay green while the operator again sees the misleading size/malformed message.

coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering finish_reason threading at the three render sites.
